reason: The hypothesis synthesizes two separate findings—the heterogeneous F/N-rich passivation film from pickling (P1, P4) and the temperature-enhanced uniform passivation in SCP solution (P9, P11)—into a new mechanistic proposal that controlled annealing can homogenize the film and improve corrosion resistance across both room-temperature and high-temperature regimes. No passage proposes annealing pre-exposed Q235 steel to convert residual pickling species into a uniform oxide, nor links film heterogeneity to chloride penetration in this way.
copied_elements: Q235 steel with pickling/passivation film containing F and N (P1, P4)
passivation film rupture and pitting in salt spray (P2, P3, P5)
temperature accelerates passivation and forms better/thicker Fe2O3 film in SCP solution (P9, P11, P26)
EIS, XPS, SEM, weight loss as characterization methods (P1, P3, P4, P9, P14, P18)
